reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about dislocation blocking, back-stress generation, and their effect on creep in CrMnFeCoNi multilayers, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge covers general dislocation-interface interactions, but the specific application to this HEA system and creep conditions requires supporting citations, which are absent.
premises: Incoherent or semi-coherent interfaces in HEA multilayers block dislocation motion
Dislocation pile-up at interfaces generates a back-stress that inhibits further plastic deformation
Reduced dislocation propagation across layers leads to lower creep rates
Creep resistance depends on interface spacing and degree of incoherency
Monolithic HEA coatings serve as a valid baseline for comparison
